claims.text: On September 22nd, UTMB and OpenEvidence announced a collaboration that gives UTMB clinicians cited medical evidence from within the electronic health record.
claims.quote:
September 22, 2026
The University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) and OpenEvidence today announced a collaboration that brings evidence-based artificial intelligence directly into clinicians' everyday workflows, giving UTMB physicians and other clinical users secure access to cited medical evidence from within the electronic health record.
claims.scope_note: UTMB's own release. The page prints the dateline September 22, 2026 above the body, and the quote now carries it so the spoken date traces to the claim. The electronic health record vendor isn't named. Matches docket tx-2026-0208-c1.
claims.verification: Independent validator (Opus) re-fetched the live page. The director's own fetch saved the snapshot and confirmed each quote fragment appears verbatim in it. Quote widened by the director after the builder's gate defect D1 to include the page's own dateline, confirmed verbatim in the saved snapshot and by the validator's fragment check.

claims.text: The integration went live at UTMB in March.
claims.quote: The integration, which went live at UTMB in March, was developed to give clinicians access to AI-enabled information resources within existing clinical workflows.
claims.scope_note: Month only, no day. Matches docket c2.
claims.verification: Independent validator (Opus) re-fetched the live page. The director's own fetch saved the snapshot and confirmed each quote fragment appears verbatim in it.

claims.text: UTMB clinicians reach the platform with their standard UTMB enterprise credentials.
claims.quote: Clinicians access the platform using their standard UTMB enterprise credentials.
claims.scope_note: Describes how clinicians sign in. Says nothing about patients or any screen. Matches docket c3.
claims.verification: Independent validator (Opus) re-fetched the live page. The director's own fetch saved the snapshot and confirmed each quote fragment appears verbatim in it.

claims.text: Clinicians ask clinical questions in plain language and receive answers that include citations to medical literature, clinical guidelines and other sources.
claims.quote: Once authenticated, clinicians can ask clinical questions in natural language and receive responses that include citations to medical literature, clinical guidelines, and other authoritative sources.
claims.scope_note: The mechanism as UTMB describes it. A citation shows where an answer says it came from, not that the answer is right. The live page uses single spaces around authoritative where docket c4 has double spaces.
claims.verification: Independent validator (Opus) re-fetched the live page. The director's own fetch saved the snapshot and confirmed each quote fragment appears verbatim in it.

claims.text: UTMB says more than half of its clinicians actively use OpenEvidence for clinical decision support.
claims.quote: Today, more than half of UTMB clinicians actively use OpenEvidence for clinical decision support.
claims.scope_note: UTMB's own report, not checked by anyone else. The release gives no clinician count, no definition of active use, no measurement period and no method. More than half is the release's own wording, so no figure was derived.
claims.verification: Independent validator (Opus) re-fetched the live page. The director's own fetch saved the snapshot and confirmed each quote fragment appears verbatim in it.

claims.text: UTMB says it will keep evaluating use and clinician experience, and its release publishes no measure of whether the answers are accurate or whether patient care changed.
claims.quote: As adoption grows, UTMB will continue evaluating utilization, clinician experience, and opportunities to improve how evidence and clinical intelligence are delivered at the point of care.
claims.scope_note: The validator searched the release for any accuracy, error-rate, validation, outcome, patient-care, safety or independent-evaluation figure and found none. The release does not mention telling patients. Matches docket c7.
claims.verification: Independent validator (Opus) re-fetched the live page. The director's own fetch saved the snapshot and confirmed each quote fragment appears verbatim in it.

claims.text: Under Texas Health and Safety Code Section 183.005, a health care practitioner may use artificial intelligence for diagnostic purposes if conditions are met, including review of all records it creates.
claims.quote:
A health care practitioner may use artificial intelligence for diagnostic purposes, including the use of artificial intelligence for recommendations on a diagnosis or course of treatment based on a patient's medical record, if:
the practitioner reviews all records created with artificial intelligence
claims.scope_note: Legal background only. The section does not mention clinical decision support. No source says a UTMB OpenEvidence question counts as diagnostic use.
claims.verification: Independent validator (Opus) re-fetched the live page. The director's own fetch saved the snapshot and confirmed each quote fragment appears verbatim in it.

claims.text: The same section requires a practitioner who uses artificial intelligence for diagnostic purposes to disclose that use to patients.
claims.quote: A health care practitioner who uses artificial intelligence for diagnostic purposes as described by Subsection (a) must disclose the practitioner's use of that technology to the practitioner's patients.
claims.scope_note: Legal background only. No source says whether this applies to UTMB's use or whether UTMB tells patients.
claims.verification: Independent validator (Opus) re-fetched the live page. The director's own fetch saved the snapshot and confirmed each quote fragment appears verbatim in it.

claims.text: Under a Texas law in effect since January 1st, 2026, a provider that uses an artificial intelligence system in a health care service must disclose it to the patient by the date the service is first provided, except in an emergency.
claims.quote: If an artificial intelligence system is used in relation to health care service or treatment, the provider of the service or treatment shall provide the disclosure under Subsection (b) to the recipient of the service or treatment or the recipient's personal representative not later than the date the service or treatment is first provided, except in the case of emergency
claims.source_type: primary_official (enrolled H.B. 149, Business and Commerce Code Sec. 552.051(f))
claims.scope_note: Legal background only. The section does not define provider or say whether it covers tools used only by staff. No source says how UTMB handles it.
claims.verification: Independent validator (Opus) re-fetched the live page. The director's own fetch saved the snapshot and confirmed each quote fragment appears verbatim in it.

rejected.claim: Abridge's enterprise framework lets UT health institutions, including UTMB, access its tool (docket tx-2026-0210)
rejected.reason: Only the vendor says it. The vendor page lists UT Medical Branch as one UT System institution without saying UTMB uses the tool. The UT System page does not name Abridge. No UT System source confirms it.

rejected.claim: UTMB clinicians in Galveston County use the tool
rejected.reason: The release body does not place clinicians, campuses or the integration in Galveston County. The county is the Docket's editorial placement, and the institution's full name includes Galveston.

rejected.claim: Texas law permits AI for diagnostic purposes with no conditions (researcher paraphrase of S.B. 1188)
rejected.reason: The statute allows it only under conditions, so the claim states them. The researcher's joined quote with an ellipsis dropped them.

rejected.claim: Other  authoritative  sources with double spaces (researcher and docket c4 quote)
rejected.reason: The live page text uses single spaces, so the verbatim quote is corrected.

rejected.claim: The UT System Board of Regents meets in public and takes testimony on agenda topics
rejected.reason: No source fetched in this pass supports it, so it is not a film claim.

rejected.claim: A clinician asks a question without leaving the record
rejected.reason: Without leaving is not verbatim. The supported wording is from within the electronic health record (c1).
